final_note: You worked through the key terms in Nucleic Acids.

concepts.def: The monomer of a nucleic acid, made of a pentose sugar, a phosphate group and one nitrogenous base (adenine, guanine, cytosine, thymine or uracil).
The two strands of a DNA double helix run in opposite directions, 5-prime to 3-prime and 3-prime to 5-prime, held together by hydrogen bonds between bases.
Adenine pairs with thymine by two hydrogen bonds and guanine pairs with cytosine by three hydrogen bonds in DNA.
DNA copying in which each new molecule keeps one original template strand and one newly made strand, as shown by Meselson and Stahl.
A length of DNA wound around a core of eight histone proteins, helping to package DNA and to regulate transcription in eukaryotes.
The synthesis of a complementary mRNA strand from a DNA template by RNA polymerase, which is the first stage of gene expression.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Nucleic Acids — a core area of Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Nucleic Acids brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Nucleic Acids.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In DNA, adenine forms hydrogen bonds with:
options: thymine
guanine
cytosine
uracil

mcqs.q: The two strands of DNA are antiparallel, which means they:
options: run in opposite 5-prime to 3-prime directions
are exactly the same length
carry identical base sequences
repel each other

mcqs.q: DNA replication is semi-conservative because each new molecule contains:
options: one original strand and one new strand
two completely new strands
two original strands
only the original strands

mcqs.q: A nucleosome consists of DNA wound around:
options: a core of histone proteins
a single RNA molecule
a ribosome
a centriole

mcqs.q: Why are DNA's two strands described as antiparallel?
options: Antiparallel just means the two strands are the same length.
The strands run in opposite directions, one 5-prime to 3-prime and the other 3-prime to 5-prime, which is required for base pairing and replication.
Guanine pairs with adenine using three hydrogen bonds.
Antiparallel means the strands repel each other.

mcqs.q: In semi-conservative replication, what does each new DNA molecule contain?
options: Each new molecule has one original template strand and one newly synthesised strand.
Each new DNA molecule is made entirely of brand-new strands.
The original DNA stays intact while a fully separate copy is built.
Antiparallel means the strands repel each other.

mcqs.q: How many hydrogen bonds hold guanine and cytosine together?
options: All base pairs are held by the same number of hydrogen bonds.
Guanine and cytosine pair with three hydrogen bonds, while adenine and thymine pair with two.
Antiparallel means the strands repel each other.
Guanine pairs with adenine using three hydrogen bonds.
